articles.summary_en: This post highlights GitHub's rapid platform growth, citing data from COO Kyle Daigle. It specifically notes a massive increase in commit activity and the doubling of GitHub Actions usage minutes.
articles.summary_zh: 本文引用 GitHub 營運長 Kyle Daigle 的數據，強調 GitHub 平台的快速成長。內容特別指出程式碼提交數量的巨幅增長，以及 GitHub Actions 使用時數在兩年內翻倍的驚人趨勢。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content focuses on reporting specific growth statistics and platform usage metrics.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容主要聚焦於報導具體的平台成長數據與使用指標。

articles.title: Vulnerability Research Is Cooked
articles.summary_en: Thomas Ptacek argues that AI coding agents are poised to revolutionize vulnerability research by automating exploit discovery. By leveraging vast pattern-matching capabilities and relentless search processes, these models can identify zero-day vulnerabilities more efficiently than traditional methods.
articles.summary_zh: Thomas Ptacek 指出，AI 編碼代理將透過自動化漏洞挖掘徹底改變安全研究領域。憑藉強大的模式匹配能力與不間斷的搜尋效率，這些模型能比傳統方法更有效地發現零時差漏洞。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article discusses the conceptual shift in the field of cybersecurity caused by the emergence of AI agents in vulnerability discovery.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文探討了 AI 代理在漏洞挖掘領域的出現，所導致的網路安全概念性轉變。

articles.title: The cognitive impact of coding agents
articles.summary_en: Simon Willison shares a viral short-form video clip from his appearance on Lenny Rachitsky's podcast. The post explores the cognitive impact of using coding agents and touches on the broader implications of AI engineering.
articles.summary_zh: Simon Willison 分享了他參與 Lenny Rachitsky 播客的一段熱門短影音。本文探討了使用程式編寫代理（coding agents）對認知造成的影響，並觸及了 AI 工程領域的相關議題。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content focuses on the conceptual discussion regarding the cognitive impacts and implications of using AI coding agents.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容重點在於探討使用 AI 程式編寫代理所帶來的認知影響與相關概念性議題。

articles.title: The Mystery of Rennes-le-Château, Part 3: A Secret History
articles.summary_en: This article explores the historical and pseudo-historical origins of Rennes-le-Château, focusing on the investigation by Henry Lincoln. It serves as part of a series examining the real-world research that inspired the game Gabriel Knight 3.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了雷恩堡（Rennes-le-Château）的歷史與偽歷史背景，重點介紹了亨利·林肯（Henry Lincoln）的相關調查。這篇文章是探討啟發電子遊戲《狩魔獵人3：血色神聖》現實研究系列的一部分。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article provides historical context and explanations regarding the background of a specific mystery and its connection to a game.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文提供了關於特定謎團的歷史背景與解釋，以及其與遊戲之間的關聯。

articles.title: The Reckoning
articles.summary_en: The author reflects on the societal 'reckoning' brought about by AI, criticizing how its marketing has focused on existential threats and displacement rather than utility. The post contrasts the hyper-individualism of the US with the communal cohesion observed in Hong Kong, arguing for structural improvements to restore social trust.
articles.summary_zh: 作者反思了人工智慧帶來的社會「清算」，批評其行銷策略過度渲染威脅與生存危機，而非強調實用價值。文章對比了美國的極端個人主義與香港的社會凝聚力，呼籲透過改善社會環境來重建信任。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article explores the conceptual shifts in societal structure and the philosophical implications of AI development.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文探討了社會結構的概念性轉變以及人工智慧發展所帶來的哲學意涵。

articles.title: Em Dashes: Back In Style?
articles.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
articles.summary_en: The author reflects on their long-term struggle to maintain a massive, legacy WordPress blog archive. They explore Cloudflare's new 'EmDash' tool, which aims to simplify migrating unstable WordPress sites to the modern Astro framework.
articles.summary_zh: 作者回顧了維護大型 WordPress 部落格存檔的長期挑戰。文中探討了 Cloudflare 推出的新工具「EmDash」，旨在協助使用者將不穩定的 WordPress 網站遷移至現代化的 Astro 架構。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article uses the author's personal experience with site migration as a case study for evaluating new web infrastructure tools.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文以作者個人網站遷移的經驗作為案例，探討並評估了新型網路基礎架構工具的應用。

articles.title: Package Manager Easter Eggs
articles.summary_en: This article explores the long-standing tradition of hidden easter eggs within various software package managers. It showcases specific examples, such as the 'moo' commands in apt, aptitude, and zypper, which reveal creative ASCII art and playful interactions.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了軟體套件管理工具中隱藏彩蛋的悠久傳統。文中介紹了 apt、aptitude 和 zypper 等工具中著名的「moo」指令，展示了這些隱藏功能所呈現的 ASCII 藝術與趣味互動。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article serves as a curated list and historical reference of easter eggs found in software tools.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文彙整了軟體工具中隱藏彩蛋的清單，屬於參考性質的資訊紀錄。

articles.title: The "Passive Income" trap ate a generation of entrepreneurs
articles.summary_en: The article critiques the trend of entrepreneurs pursuing 'passive income' through low-value ventures like dropshipping. It suggests that many such business models lack genuine innovation and long-term sustainability.
articles.summary_zh: 本文批評了企業家透過「被動收入」追求低價值業務（如代發貨）的趨勢。文章指出，許多這類商業模式缺乏真正的創新與長期可持續性。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article uses an anecdotal story about a specific business model to illustrate a broader critique of the 'passive income' trap.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 文章透過關於特定商業模式的軼事，來闡述對「被動收入」陷阱的廣泛批判。

articles.title: Roman moon, Greek moon
articles.summary_en: The article explains the terminology used for the closest approach to the moon, noting the interchangeability of 'perilune' and 'periselene'. It clarifies that the terms are derived from Roman and Greek roots for the moon, respectively.
articles.summary_zh: 本文解釋了用於描述月球近地點的術語，指出「perilune」與「periselene」可以互換使用。文中並說明這兩個詞彙分別源自羅馬與希臘語中對月球的稱呼。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post provides a conceptual explanation and definition of astronomical terminology.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 該文章提供了天文學術語的概念性解釋與定義。

articles.title: Hyperbolic version of Napier’s mnemonic
articles.summary_en: The author explores a hyperbolic analog to Napier's mnemonic, a tool traditionally used in spherical trigonometry. While noting that hyperbolic analogs exist for most geometric concepts, the author highlights this specific discovery as a unique mathematical curiosity.
articles.summary_zh: 作者探討了納皮爾助記法（Napier’s mnemonic）的雙曲幾何模擬版本，這是一種傳統上用於球面三角學的工具。作者指出，雖然雙曲幾何中存在大多數幾何概念的模擬形式，但這一發現仍具備獨特的數學趣味。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content explains and reflects on a mathematical concept rather than providing a tutorial or specific data set.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容旨在解釋與探討一個數學概念，而非提供操作教學或特定的數據集。

articles.title: How can I use Read­Directory­ChangesW to know when someone is copying a file out of the directory?
articles.summary_en: This post clarifies that file copying is not a distinct file system operation, making it impossible to detect directly via ReadDirectoryChangesW. It explains that since copying is just a series of read and write operations, the file system cannot distinguish it from other file access patterns.
articles.summary_zh: 本文指出「複製檔案」並非底層檔案系統的基本運作，因此無法透過 ReadDirectoryChangesW 直接偵測。作者解釋由於複製過程僅是多次讀取與寫入的組合，檔案系統無法將其與其他操作區隔開來。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article explains a conceptual limitation of file systems regarding how they handle copy operations.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文旨在解釋檔案系統在處理複製操作時的概念性限制與運作機制。

articles.title: Book Review: Superintelligence - Paths, Dangers, Strategies by Nick Bostrom ★★★★⯪
articles.summary_en: This review discusses Nick Bostrom's 2014 book, Superintelligence, highlighting its profound analysis of the existential risks associated with true artificial intelligence. The author emphasizes the book's foresight in outlining necessary safety measures and conceptual frameworks long before current AI advancements.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇書評探討了尼克·博斯特羅姆（Nick Bostrom）於 2014 年出版的《超級智慧》，強調其對人工智慧潛在生存風險的深刻分析。作者特別指出該書在當前 AI 技術發展之前，就已精準預見了必要的安全防範措施與理論框架。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content focuses on analyzing the theoretical risks and conceptual implications of superintelligent AI.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容重點在於分析超級人工智慧的理論風險及其概念意涵。

articles.title: My Zip bomb strategy is not as effective as it used to be
articles.summary_en: The author discusses the declining effectiveness of using zip bombs to neutralize malicious web bots. While previously a reliable defense for a modest server setup, the author notes that modern, more sophisticated bots are increasingly able to circumvent this mitigation strategy.
articles.summary_zh: 作者探討了利用 ZIP 炸彈來防禦惡意網路爬蟲的效果逐漸降低的問題。儘管過去這是在小型伺服器上應對攻擊的有效手段，但作者指出，現代且更聰明的機器人已開始能繞過此類防禦機制。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post functions as a case study reflecting on the author's real-world experimental results with a specific server defense strategy.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於案例研究，反映了作者在伺服器防禦策略上的實務經驗與實驗結果。

articles.title: Quoting Willy Tarreau
articles.summary_en: Willy Tarreau reports a massive increase in Linux kernel security vulnerability reports, rising from a few per week to 5-10 per day. This surge is largely attributed to AI tools, which have improved detection efficiency to the point of generating frequent duplicate findings.
articles.summary_zh: Willy Tarreau 指出 Linux 核心安全漏洞報告數量大幅增加，從過去每週數件飆升至每日 5 到 10 件。這波成長主要歸因於 AI 工具的普及，這些工具顯著提升了偵測效率，甚至導致多人同時發現相同漏洞的情況頻繁發生。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content presents empirical observations and data regarding the impact of AI tools on security reporting workflows.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容呈現了關於 AI 工具對安全通報流程影響的實證觀察與數據。

articles.title: Quoting Daniel Stenberg
articles.summary_en: Daniel Stenberg, the lead developer of cURL, discusses the changing impact of AI on open source security. He notes a shift from an influx of AI-generated 'slop' to a high volume of legitimate, high-quality security reports that require significant manual review.
articles.summary_zh: cURL 專案負責人 Daniel Stenberg 分享了 AI 對開源軟體安全帶來的影響。他指出，目前的挑戰已從大量的 AI 生成廢話轉變為海量的優質安全報告，導致維護者需要投入大量時間進行審核。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content serves as a real-world, first-hand account or case study from a maintainer on the practical impact of AI tools in security workflows.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容提供了來自專案維護者的第一手觀察與案例，說明 AI 工具對實際安全工作流程的影響。

articles.title: Quoting Greg Kroah-Hartman
articles.summary_en: Linux kernel maintainer Greg Kroah-Hartman notes a significant shift in AI-generated security reports. Initially dismissed as low-quality 'slop,' AI tools are now producing accurate and actionable security analysis for open-source projects.
articles.summary_zh: Linux 核心維護者 Greg Kroah-Hartman 指出，AI 生成的安全報告已發生顯著變化。起初被視為低品質的「垃圾內容」，現在 AI 工具已能為開源專案提供準確且具備實用價值的安全性分析。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content presents expert testimony acting as evidence of the evolving state and effectiveness of AI in security research.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 該內容引述了專家的觀點，作為 AI 在安全研究領域中應用進展與有效性的證據。

articles.title: Can JavaScript Escape a CSP Meta Tag Inside an Iframe?
articles.summary_en: This post investigates whether JavaScript can bypass Content Security Policy (CSP) meta tags injected within sandboxed iframes. The author demonstrates that these meta tags are effectively enforced by the browser even when subsequent untrusted JavaScript attempts to modify them.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章探討了 JavaScript 是否能繞過沙盒 iframe 內嵌入的內容安全策略（CSP）meta 標籤。作者實證說明，即使後續的不受信任腳本嘗試進行竄改，瀏覽器仍會強制執行這些 meta 標籤。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content is based on the author's specific research and practical experiment regarding browser behavior.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容基於作者針對瀏覽器行為的特定研究與實驗結果。

articles.title: The Axios supply chain attack used individually targeted social engineering
articles.summary_en: Axios maintainers released a postmortem detailing a sophisticated supply chain attack that targeted a developer through highly personalized social engineering. The attackers impersonated company leadership and used fake professional environments to trick the maintainer into installing malware during a video conference.
articles.summary_zh: Axios 團隊發布了一份事故調查報告，詳細說明一起針對維護者的複雜供應鏈攻擊，該攻擊利用高度客製化的社交工程手段進行。攻擊者偽裝成公司創辦人並建立專業的虛假環境，誘騙維護者在視訊會議期間安裝惡意軟體。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article functions as a postmortem case study, providing a real-world account of a security incident.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於事故調查報告的案例研究，提供了資安事件的真實發生經過。

articles.title: Build your own Dial-up ISP with a Raspberry Pi
articles.summary_en: This article explores the technical history of the iBook G3 and its significance as the first consumer laptop with built-in Wi-Fi. It sets the stage for a project involving legacy hardware connectivity and the creation of a dial-up ISP using a Raspberry Pi.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了 iBook G3 的技術歷史，以及其作為首款內建 Wi-Fi 功能的消費級筆記型電腦的重要性。文章為後續利用 Raspberry Pi 建立撥接網路服務提供商 (ISP) 的硬體連接專案奠定了基礎。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article introduces a technical project aimed at building a specific system, categorizing it as a procedural guide.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文介紹了一個旨在建立特定系統的技術專案，屬於操作指南類型的內容。

articles.title: Programming (with AI agents) as theory building
articles.summary_en: This article explores the concept of programming not as mere instruction-giving, but as the active construction of mental models and theories. It suggests that integrating AI agents into the development process shifts the developer's role toward architecting these theoretical frameworks.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章探討了程式設計不僅僅是下達指令，而是構建心智模型與理論的過程。文中指出，將 AI 代理整合進開發流程，能讓開發者的角色轉變為這些理論框架的建構者。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article focuses on the theoretical framing and conceptual definition of programming as a process of building theories.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文側重於將程式設計定義為構建理論的過程，屬於概念性與理論探討的範疇。

articles.title: SQLAlchemy 2 In Practice - Chapter 3 - One-To-Many Relationships
articles.summary_en: This article serves as the third chapter of Miguel Grinberg's book on SQLAlchemy 2, focusing on implementing one-to-many relationships. It follows a previous discussion on product queries, transitioning into managing data associations between entities.
articles.summary_zh: 本文是 Miguel Grinberg 所著 SQLAlchemy 2 實踐書籍的第三章，重點探討如何實作「一對多」關聯。內容延續前一章關於產品查詢的討論，進一步引導讀者處理資料表之間的關聯映射。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content is part of a practical guide that teaches implementation steps for database relationships in SQLAlchemy.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於實作指南的一部分，教授如何在 SQLAlchemy 中執行資料庫關聯的具體設定步驟。

articles.title: The Blandness of Systematic Rules vs. The Delight of Localized Sensitivity
articles.summary_en: This post explores the tension between adhering to rigid systematic UI design rules and the value of localized, context-aware design choices. The author argues that while systematic rules promote consistency, thoughtful exceptions can provide a level of delight and clarity that universal guidelines sometimes stifle, especially as software scales.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了嚴格遵守系統化 UI 設計準則與採用局部、情境化設計決策之間的衝突。作者認為，雖然系統化規則能確保一致性，但在設計中加入經過深思熟慮的例外處理，往往能創造出更具吸引力且直觀的體驗，特別是在軟體擴展時，盲目追求系統化反而可能扼殺設計的靈活度。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article discusses the conceptual tension between systematic design rules and localized sensitivity, focusing on design philosophy rather than a how-to or empirical study.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文探討了系統化設計規則與局部靈敏度之間的理論衝突，重點在於設計理念的探討，而非操作指南或實證研究。

articles.title: Information and Technological Evolution
articles.summary_en: This article explores the nature of technological progress and critiques the quality of existing literature on the subject. It highlights the author's ongoing interest in understanding how information and technology evolve over time.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討技術進步的本質，並對現有關於該主題的文獻質量進行了評論。作者分享了其長期以來對資訊與技術隨時間演進過程的研究興趣。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content focuses on theoretical reflection and the conceptual nature of technological evolution.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容側重於理論性反思以及技術演進的概念本質。

articles.title: Time is a User-Interface
articles.summary_en: This article explores the concept of time as a fundamental component of user interface design. It examines how temporal dynamics and sequencing influence user experience and interaction patterns.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討時間作為使用者介面設計中一項基礎要素的概念。文中分析了時間動態與順序安排如何影響使用者體驗及互動模式。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article discusses a conceptual framework regarding the role of time in design rather than a tutorial or data-heavy report.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文旨在探討時間在設計中的角色，屬於概念性框架分析，而非操作指南或數據報告。

articles.title: Artemis II, Apollo 8, and Apollo 13
articles.summary_en: The article compares the Artemis II mission to the historic Apollo 8 and Apollo 13 missions. It highlights similarities in mission objectives, specifically the lunar flyby trajectory used to prepare for future moon landings.
articles.summary_zh: 本文比較了 Artemis II 任務與歷史上的阿波羅 8 號及 13 號任務。重點在於它們在任務目標上的相似性，特別是透過繞月飛行來為未來的登月任務做準備。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article primarily functions by drawing direct parallels between current space missions and historical precedents.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文的主要內容是透過對比當前的太空任務與歷史任務來進行說明。

articles.title: Why doesn’t the system let you declare your own messages to have the same semantics as WM_COPY­DATA?
articles.summary_en: This post explains why developers cannot replicate the unique cross-process memory semantics of WM_COPYDATA for custom Windows messages. It highlights that the system imposes strict limitations to ensure security and prevent memory corruption during inter-process communication.
articles.summary_zh: 本文解釋了為何開發者無法為自定義視窗訊息複製 WM_COPYDATA 的跨處理序記憶體語義。文中指出，系統實施嚴格限制是為了確保安全性並防止處理序間通訊過程中的記憶體損壞。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post provides a conceptual explanation of why the Windows system enforces specific architectural constraints on message handling.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文對為何 Windows 系統在處理訊息時執行特定的架構限制提供了概念性的解釋。

articles.title: Concert Review: London Philharmonic - Pictures at an Exhibition ★★★★★
articles.summary_en: This blog post provides a personal review of a London Philharmonic concert featuring works by Mark-Anthony Turnage and Béla Bartók. The author highlights the emotional intensity and chaotic nature of the performance, specifically praising the inventive delivery of 'Three Screaming Popes'.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇部落格文章回顧了倫敦愛樂樂團的音樂會，內容涵蓋馬克-安東尼·圖爾內奇與巴爾托克的作品。作者分享了對演出情感張力的個人見解，特別讚賞了《三個尖叫的教宗》中充滿創意且混亂狂野的演繹。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content acts as a personal reflection and descriptive critique of a musical performance, focusing on the subjective experience and conceptual interpretation of the pieces.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容屬於對音樂會的個人感想與敘事性評論，重點在於作者的主觀感受與對作品的概念詮釋。

articles.title: Random File Format
articles.summary_en: The author explores a concept for a resilient file format capable of playing back content even if the file is incomplete or corrupted. This idea was inspired by common issues with truncated media downloads during the early 2000s.
articles.summary_zh: 作者探討了一種具備強韌性的檔案格式構想，即使在檔案不完整或毀損的情況下仍能正常播放內容。此概念源自於 2000 年代初期下載媒體檔案時，常見因檔案截斷而導致無法讀取的技術問題。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article discusses a theoretical concept for file architecture and potential problem-solving for data corruption.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文探討了關於檔案架構的理論概念，以及針對資料毀損問題的潛在解決方案。

articles.title: Pluralistic: It's extremely good that Claude's source-code leaked (02 Apr 2026)
articles.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
articles.summary_en: Cory Doctorow discusses the recent leak of Anthropic's Claude Code due to a configuration error and critiques the company's use of DMCA takedown notices. The article highlights the legal complexities of copyright law, particularly how strict liability impacts intermediaries and platforms.
articles.summary_zh: Cory Doctorow 探討了 Anthropic 因配置錯誤導致 Claude Code 原始碼外洩的事件，並批評該公司濫用數位千禧年著作權法（DMCA）發送下架通知。文章進一步分析了版權法中的「嚴格責任」原則如何對網路中介平台造成法律壓力。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article explains the legal theory behind copyright liability and the function of DMCA 512, focusing on the conceptual implications of the leak.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 文章解釋了版權法律責任的理論基礎以及 DMCA 512 條款的功能，重點在於分析原始碼外洩後的法律概念意涵。

articles.title: 13th Year of Blogging
articles.summary_en: The author reflects on thirteen years of blogging, highlighting the challenges of technical maintenance and the importance of perseverance. They argue that personal experience and long-term consistency create a unique value that AI-generated content cannot replicate.
articles.summary_zh: 作者回顧了部落格經營十三年的歷程，強調了維護技術架構的挑戰以及堅持不懈的重要性。作者認為，個人經歷與長期的耕耘積累了 AI 生成內容所無法複製的獨特價值。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article uses the metaphor of growing an oak tree to illustrate the value of longevity in blogging compared to AI-generated content.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 文章使用了種植橡樹的隱喻，藉此說明部落格的長期價值遠勝於 AI 生成內容。

articles.title: Spring 2026 Pebble App Contest + SDK Updates
articles.summary_en: Eric Migicovsky has announced the Spring 2026 Pebble App Contest to celebrate the start of mass production for the Pebble Time 2. The post invites developers to participate while highlighting upcoming updates to the Pebble SDK.
articles.summary_zh: Eric Migicovsky 宣佈舉辦 2026 年春季 Pebble 應用程式競賽，以慶祝 Pebble Time 2 正式進入量產階段。文中同時預告了 Pebble SDK 的即將更新，並邀請開發者參與競賽。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article announces a competition and provides guidance/updates for developers, serving as a procedural call to action.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文旨在宣佈競賽活動並為開發者提供指引與更新，屬於程序性的行動呼籲。

articles.title: Highlights from my conversation about agentic engineering on Lenny's Podcast
articles.summary_en: Simon Willison shares highlights from his guest appearance on Lenny's Podcast, where he discusses the current state of AI and agentic engineering. The post covers key topics including the AI inflection point, the evolving role of software engineers, and the rise of automated 'dark factories'.
articles.summary_zh: Simon Willison 分享了他參與 Lenny 播客的重點摘要，探討 AI 與代理人工程（Agentic Engineering）的現況。文中涵蓋了 AI 的轉折點、軟體工程師角色的演變，以及自動化「黑暗工廠」的興起等核心議題。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content provides a conceptual overview and high-level insights regarding the impact of AI on industry and engineering practices.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 該內容提供了關於 AI 對產業及工程實踐影響的概念性概述與高層級見解。

articles.title: Gemma 4: Byte for byte, the most capable open models
articles.summary_en: Google has released Gemma 4, a series of open-weights vision-capable models ranging from 2B to 31B parameters, featuring a novel Per-Layer Embedding technique to enhance efficiency. Simon Willison provides a brief technical overview of the architecture and shares his hands-on experience testing these models via LM Studio.
articles.summary_zh: Google 發布了 Gemma 4 系列開源視覺語言模型，參數規模涵蓋 2B 到 31B，並採用了創新的「每層嵌入」(Per-Layer Embeddings) 技術以提升參數效率。作者 Simon Willison 在文中簡述了其架構特點，並分享了透過 LM Studio 進行實測的心得。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post provides firsthand testing, observations, and benchmarks regarding the performance and functionality of new AI models.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 文章提供了針對新款 AI 模型的實測觀察與效能驗證，屬於基於證據的評測內容。

articles.title: llm-gemini 0.30
articles.summary_en: Simon Willison has released version 0.30 of the llm-gemini tool. This update adds support for new Google models including gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview and the Gemma 4 family.
articles.summary_zh: Simon Willison 發布了 llm-gemini 工具的 0.30 版本。此次更新增加了對 Google 新模型（如 gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview 和 Gemma 4 系列）的支援。
articles.pacer_reason_en: This post serves as a release announcement and reference for updated software specifications and model availability.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 此文章為軟體版本更新公告，主要作為軟體規格與模型支援情況的參考資訊。

articles.title: March 2026 sponsors-only newsletter
articles.summary_en: Simon Willison has released his March 2026 sponsors-only newsletter, covering topics such as agentic engineering, local LLM streaming on Mac, and recent software supply chain security issues. This monthly publication offers exclusive insights and technical updates for his GitHub sponsors.
articles.summary_zh: Simon Willison 發布了 2026 年 3 月的贊助者專屬電子報，內容涵蓋代理工程模式、在 Mac 上串流專家模型，以及 PyPI 和 NPM 的供應鏈攻擊等主題。該電子報每月為其 GitHub 贊助者提供獨家的技術見解與專案更新。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content acts primarily as a notification and reference guide for accessing exclusive subscriber-only materials.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 此內容主要作為存取訂閱者專屬資料的通知與參考指南。

articles.title: datasette-llm 0.1a6
articles.summary_en: The datasette-llm 0.1a6 release introduces a quality-of-life update where default models are automatically added to the allowed models list. It also includes improved documentation for the tool's Python API usage.
articles.summary_zh: datasette-llm 0.1a6 版本發布，現在將模型設為預設值時會自動加入允許列表，無需重複設定。此外，該版本還增強了 Python API 的使用說明文件。

articles.title: datasette-enrichments-llm 0.2a1
articles.summary_en: Simon Willison has released version 0.2a1 of the datasette-enrichments-llm plugin. This update introduces the passing of the 'actor' parameter to the llm.mode method when triggering an enrichment.
articles.summary_zh: Simon Willison 發布了 datasette-enrichments-llm 外掛程式的 0.2a1 版本。此次更新讓觸發豐富化處理時，能將 'actor' 參數傳遞給 llm.mode 方法。
articles.pacer_reason_en: This is a software release note detailing specific changes and updates to a library.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 這是一份軟體發布說明，詳細列出了函式庫的具體變更與更新內容。

articles.title: On the Vergecast, On Video
articles.summary_en: Anil Dash reflects on his guest appearance on The Vergecast, where he discussed the importance of keeping podcasting an open ecosystem. He also highlights a segment featuring Jason Snell, who provides a critical analysis of Apple's 50-year history and its recent moral shortcomings.
articles.summary_zh: Anil Dash 分享了他參與 The Vergecast 的心得，討論了保持播客生態開放的重要性。此外，他還推薦了節目中關於蘋果 50 週年歷史的深度分析，特別是 Jason Snell 對蘋果近期道德失誤的直率評論。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article is primarily conceptual, discussing the principles of open podcasting and commentary on industry shifts rather than being a guide or data report.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文主要探討開放式播客的理念以及對產業趨勢的評論，屬於觀念性內容，而非教學指南或數據報告。

articles.title: Mini-review: David Pogue's Apple: The First 50 Years
articles.summary_en: This review evaluates David Pogue's book, 'Apple: The First 50 Years,' comparing it to previous historical accounts like 'Apple Confidential.' The reviewer finds that, despite initial skepticism, the book provides a surprisingly deep technical dive into Apple's early history, including the Apple-1, Apple III, and the development of the Macintosh.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇書評探討了 David Pogue 所著的《Apple: The First 50 Years》，並將其與《Apple Confidential》等經典著作進行了對比。書評作者最初對該書的深度持保留態度，但閱讀後發現該書對蘋果早期歷史，包括 Apple-1、Apple III 以及麥金塔電腦的開發過程，提供了出乎意料且詳盡的技術性回顧。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article functions as a critical review, providing evidence and evaluation of the book's content quality and historical accuracy.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於書評類內容，透過對書籍內容品質與歷史準確性的評估，提供了相關的證據與分析。

articles.title: Summary of reading: January - March 2026
articles.summary_en: This blog post provides a quarterly digest of book summaries covering various topics including political theory, geopolitics, primatology, and martial arts history. The author offers brief critical reviews, assessing the value and limitations of each work.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章整理了作者 2026 年第一季的閱讀摘要，涵蓋政治理論、地緣政治、靈長類動物學及武術歷史等書籍。作者針對每本書提供簡短的批判性評論，分析其價值與局限性。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The content serves as a list of curated book recommendations and summaries, functioning as reference material.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 內容為精選書單與摘要列表，屬於參考性質的資訊。

articles.title: April Cools Post: New York vs Chicago Pizza
articles.summary_en: This post discusses the ongoing debate between Chicago deep-dish and New York-style pizza, arguing that the comparison is fundamentally flawed. The author shares personal insights on Chicago's culinary identity, distinguishing between authentic deep-dish and the common 'stuffed' pizza style.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章探討了芝加哥深盤披薩與紐約披薩之間的爭論，並指出兩者比較的邏輯存在本質問題。作者分享了對芝加哥飲食文化的見解，並區分了傳統深盤披薩與常見的「餡餅披薩」。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article centers on comparing two different culinary styles, drawing parallels and highlighting distinctions between them.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文的核心在於比較兩種不同的飲食風格，透過類比與對比來分析兩者之間的差異。

articles.title: Mar '26 Notes
articles.summary_en: This post summarizes the author's March 2026 exploration of algebraic graph theory through academic textbooks. It also chronicles the spontaneous creation and unexpected growth of 'Wander Console,' an open-source tool for discovering independent websites.
articles.summary_zh: 本文總結了作者在 2026 年 3 月對於代數圖論的學習心得與研究筆記。此外，作者也記錄了其開發開源工具「Wander Console」的過程，以及在工作、研究與軟體維護之間取得平衡的挑戰。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article functions as a monthly log or reference collection of personal studies and project updates.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於作者個人的每月筆記與參考紀錄，彙整了學習心得與專案進度。

articles.title: Wayne’s World
articles.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
articles.summary_en: This article profiles Ronald G. Wayne, the often-overlooked third co-founder of Apple who sold his stake after only two weeks. It explores his multifaceted life beyond Apple, highlighting his career as a polymath, artist, and his work at Atari.
articles.summary_zh: 本文介紹了蘋果公司鮮為人知的第三位共同創辦人羅納德·韋恩（Ronald G. Wayne），他僅在入股兩週後便退出了公司。文章探討了他在蘋果之外的多元人生，展示了他作為博學家、藝術家以及在雅達利（Atari）工作期間的多重身份。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article provides a biographical exploration and conceptual look at a historical figure's life and role, rather than a how-to or list.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 文章以傳記的角度深入探討歷史人物的生平與角色，屬於概念性敘述而非教學或清單。

articles.title: The Entire Internet Is a UGC Reaction Video Now
articles.summary_en: The article explores the proliferation of user-generated reaction videos and bizarre websites, framing them as signs of a fracturing digital culture. It reflects on the feeling of social decay found within these internet artifacts.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了用戶生成的反應影片與各種怪異網站的氾濫，並將其視為數位文化逐漸瓦解的徵兆。作者反思了在這些網路產物中感受到的社會契約崩解感。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article is a conceptual reflection on the state of internet culture and digital behavior.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文是對網路文化現狀與數位行為的觀念性反思。

articles.title: Say the Thing You Want
articles.summary_en: This post highlights the importance of clearly articulating professional needs and desires rather than relying on silence. It argues that avoiding direct communication is counterproductive and urges readers to speak up to achieve their goals.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章強調在職場中清楚表達個人需求的重要性，而非選擇沉默。作者主張沉默並不能解決問題，呼籲讀者勇敢發聲以達成目標。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post provides a conceptual shift in mindset regarding professional communication rather than a technical tutorial.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 這篇文章提供了關於職場溝通的心態觀念轉變，而非技術性的操作教學。

articles.title: Notes from March 2026
articles.summary_en: Evan Hahn recounts his busy March 2026, highlighting his writings on software errors, AI disclosure, and personal projects. The post also details his professional work at Ghost, contributions to Zelda Dungeon, and curated links regarding current AI trends.
articles.summary_zh: Evan Hahn 分享了他在 2026 年 3 月的繁忙行程，包括關於軟體錯誤、AI 使用準則的撰寫以及多項開發專案的進展。此外，他也記錄了在 Ghost 的工作內容、為 Zelda Dungeon 撰寫的文章以及對近期 AI 產業動態的觀察。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article functions as a monthly status report and a collection of links, acting as a personal reference for the author's recent projects and readings.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於個人月度動態報告與連結彙整，適合作為作者近期專案與閱讀清單的參考資料。

articles.title: Pentagonal numbers are truncated triangular numbers
articles.summary_en: This post explains the geometric relationship between pentagonal numbers and triangular numbers. It demonstrates how pentagonal number diagrams can be visually transformed into specific triangular number patterns.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章解釋了五角數與三角數之間的幾何關係。透過視覺化的方式，展示了五角數圖形如何轉換為特定的三角數圖形。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article focuses on explaining the conceptual and visual relationship between two mathematical number sequences.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文旨在解釋兩個數學數列之間的概念性與視覺性關聯。

articles.title: The cover of C++: The Programming Language raises questions not answered by the cover
articles.summary_en: This post discusses the iconic cover art of Bjarne Stroustrup's book, 'C++: The Programming Language.' It highlights the lack of clear context or explanation for the imagery used on the book's cover.
articles.summary_zh: 這篇文章討論了 Bjarne Stroustrup 所著《C++: The Programming Language》一書的標誌性封面設計。作者指出封面上的圖像缺乏明確的背景資訊或解釋。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The post provides a conceptual discussion and commentary on the aesthetics and context of a programming book cover.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 該文章針對程式語言書籍封面的美學與背景進行了概念性的討論與評論。

articles.title: Claude Code won April Fools Day this year
articles.summary_en: Xe Iaso highlights Claude Code's successful April Fools' Day prank, which featured a digital pet (Tamagotchi) experience. The post playfully praises the creative execution of the feature as a standout moment for the holiday.
articles.summary_zh: Xe Iaso 的部落格文章指出 Claude Code 透過推出電子寵物（Tamagotchi）體驗，成功贏得了今年愚人節的關注。作者幽默地讚賞了該功能的創意執行，認為這是今年節日中最出色的亮點之一。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article is a commentary/reflection piece describing a conceptual product execution rather than a tutorial or data-heavy report.

articles.title: GopherTree
articles.summary_en: The author discusses the Gopher protocol's structure and presents a custom minimalist Gopher client written in C. The client emphasizes a directory tree interface, effectively hiding non-standard 'informational selectors' to improve navigation and user focus.
articles.summary_zh: 作者探討了 Gopher 協定的結構，並介紹了一款以 C 語言編寫的極簡 Gopher 客戶端。該客戶端強調目錄樹介面，並隱藏了非標準的「資訊選擇器」，以提升瀏覽體驗與操作專注度。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article focuses on the implementation and functional design choices of a custom-built Gopher client, acting as a technical guide to the author's development approach.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文側重於自建 Gopher 客戶端的實作過程與功能設計選擇，如同開發方法的技術指南。

articles.title: Pluralistic: Trumpismo vs minilateralism (01 Apr 2026)
articles.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
articles.summary_en: This post explores the tension between traditional US-led globalism and the rise of 'Trumpismo,' arguing that previous international orders relied on American dominance disguised as neutral cooperation. It highlights how the US historically benefited from controlling infrastructure, currency, and data, while current political shifts threaten these systemic advantages.
articles.summary_zh: 本文探討了傳統美國主導的全球主義與「川普主義」之間的緊張關係，指出過去的國際秩序建立在偽裝成中立合作的美國霸權之上。文章強調美國過去如何透過控制基礎設施、貨幣和數據獲益，並分析當前的政治轉變如何挑戰這些體系優勢。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article provides a conceptual analysis of global geopolitical theories and critiques the nature of American economic and political power.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文對全球地緣政治理論進行了概念性分析，並批判了美國經濟與政治權力的本質。

articles.title: What is Copilot exactly?
articles.summary_en: The author recounts their attempt to improve productivity using Microsoft Copilot after being inspired by a colleague. After successfully creating automated workflows for administrative tasks, they discovered the confusion stemmed from using different versions of the tool, as their colleague was referring to the code editor version rather than the workplace assistant.
articles.summary_zh: 作者受同事啟發，嘗試使用 Microsoft Copilot 來提升工作效率，並成功將繁瑣的行政工作自動化。然而，作者隨後發現這是一場誤會，因為同事指的是程式碼編輯器版本，而非作者一直在使用的辦公助理版本。
articles.pacer_reason_en: The article functions as a personal case study on experimenting with AI tools in a professional workflow and the resulting productivity insights.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 本文屬於個人案例研究，分享了在專業工作流程中實驗 AI 工具的過程與發現，以及對生產力的洞察。

articles.title: datasette-extract 0.3a0

articles.summary_zh: Datasette-extract 0.3a0 版本正式發布，新增與 datasette-llm 的整合以進行模型配置。使用者現在可以利用「extract」功能來管理用於資料提取任務的 AI 模型。
articles.pacer_reason_en: This is a software release update detailing how to configure and utilize a new tool feature.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 這是一篇軟體更新公告，詳細說明了如何配置與使用新工具功能。

articles.title: datasette-enrichments-llm 0.2a0
articles.summary_en: The datasette-enrichments-llm plugin has been updated to version 0.2a0. This release integrates with datasette-llm to allow users to configure and manage specific AI models for data enrichment tasks.

articles.pacer_reason_en: This is a software release announcement documenting updates and configuration changes.
articles.pacer_reason_zh: 這是一則軟體版本發布公告，記錄了更新內容與設定變更。

It also adds optional detailed logging for prompts and tool calls and updates security permissions for the simple prompt page.

articles.content_snippet:
Yesterday, I had the chance to witness someone who's one of the most dedicated, competent advocates for privacy and digital rights bring that message to a whole new platform. It turns out, it's pretty delightful, especially in a moment when our civil liberties and rights online couldn't matter more!
Cindy Cohn, the executive director of the Electronic Frontier Foundation, has been a tireless fighter for protecting everyone's digital civil liberties, and I was lucky enough to get to tag along as she took the story of that work to The Daily Show yesterday. It was no surprise that the conversation was so fluent and insightful on the topic, but I think a lot of people in the audience didn't expect that it would be such a fun and even delightful conversation about a topic that is, too often, confusing or complicated or boring.
Six years ago, when I first joined  the board of the EFF,  I was already a believer in the core principles the organization stood for, but one of my biggest hopes was that the messages and mission of the entire team could just be brought to a larger audience. That couldn't have been more perfectly accomplished than seeing Cindy translate some topics that were fairly technical, or which involved fairly arcane legal concerns, and make them very accessible. And this work is vital because both the overreaching, authoritarian government, and the irresponsible, unaccountable forces of big tech are threatening our rights more than ever.

More broadly, though, the interview was also just a wonderful milestone to see at a personal level. articles.title: Continuous, Continuous, Continuous
articles.content_snippet:
Jason Gorman writes about the word “continuous” and its place in making software. We think of making software in stages (and we often assign roles to ourselves and other people based on these stages):
the design phase, the coding phase, the testing phase, the integration phase, the release phase, and so on.
However this approach to building and distributing software isn’t necessarily well-suited to an age where everything moves at breakneck speed and changes constantly. 
The moment we start writing code, we see how the design needs to change. The moment we start testing, we see how the code needs to change. The moment we integrate our changes, we see how ours or other people’s code needs to change. The moment we release working software into the world, we learn how the software needs to change.
Making software is a continuous cycle of these interconnected stages: designing, coding, testing, integrating, releasing. But the lines between these stages are very blurry, and therefore the responsibilities of people on our teams will be too.
The question is: are our cycles for these stages — and the collaborative work of the people involved in them — measured in hours or weeks? Do we complete each of these stages multiple times a day, or once every few weeks?
if we work backwards from the goal of having working software that can be shipped at any time, we inevitably arrive at the need for continuous integration, and that doesn’t work without continuous testing, and that doesn’t work if we try to design and write all the code before we do any testing. Instead, we work in micro feedback loops, progressing one small step at a time, gathering feedback throughout so we can iterate towards a good result.
Feedback on the process through the process must be evolutionary. You can’t save it all up for a post-mortem or a 1-on-1. It has to happen at the moment, evolving our understanding one piece of feedback at a time (see: Gall’s law, a complex system evolves from a simpler one).

articles.title: Clip Show
articles.content_snippet:
This is my first guest post on the blog, by our shared friend GPT-5.4

This post is an AI-generated summary of the themes that recur across the archive. It is not written in the author’s voice, and it should be read as an external reconstruction of a body of argument rather than as a new primary text.
What follows is an attempt to state, as plainly as possible, the underlying philosophical picture that organizes the blog, and to locate it within several recognizable modern traditions.

At its center is a distinction between real production and parasitic mediation. Again and again, the posts return to the claim that societies live by their capacity to produce energy, housing, software, tools, medicine, and other durable goods, while much of modern institutional life is devoted to inserting tolls between persons and these goods. Hence the recurrent hostility to finance without productive purpose, to bureaucratic layers that preserve themselves by generating complexity, and to business models that profit chiefly by controlling access rather than enlarging capacity. Money is the Map states the thesis in its most explicit form: monetary valuation is a representation of value, not value itself. Once the representation is detached from the underlying territory, the social order begins rewarding strategic position rather than genuine contribution.
This basic opposition yields a moral psychology. The admirable figure is the builder: the engineer, maintainer, fabricator, organizer, or founder who increases the stock of real capability. The contemptible figure is the rent-seeker: the actor who captures flows created by others, often while claiming a civilizing or managerial necessity. The blog’s polemical energy comes less from ordinary partisanship than from this moral sorting of persons and institutions according to whether they produce or merely extract.

articles.title: Closed Source AI = Neofeudalism
articles.content_snippet:
So this isn’t the original post I had here. The original post was AI slop, and let this be a lesson to me for posting it. It doesn’t matter if you read it and think it looks good. It’s still AI slop, and everyone else can see that. This rewritten post is the same idea, but slop-free.
Besides, “the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house”

Look, if you work in a frontier lab, I don’t blame you. You have a front row seat to the hinge of history. But consider what you are building and who it’s for.
A small handful of secretive closed source labs with a concentration of compute, talent, and deployment power will lead to a concentration of political legitimacy. You may think you want this and you are the good guys who will wield power well, but you won’t and you aren’t. Absolute power corrupts absolutely.
AI safety was always a question about if safe AI could be built in theory, not if a small group of anointed people could keep it safe for us. At least I respect Yudkowsky, consistently saying “If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies”

The cat is out of the bag. We are building it. Either if anyone builds it everyone dies, or it’s safe enough for everyone to have. And given that, I don’t accept a middle ground where the chosen few can have it. This isn’t like nuclear weapons, this is intelligence itself. A nuclear weapon can only destroy; intelligence is the greatest creative force in the world. If a small group of people have a monopoly on it, you are the permanent underclass in the same way animals are.
Open source AI isn’t anti-safety. It’s anti-feudal. Every time some AI guy blathers on about how open source is dangerous but he can build AI and make it safe (but only if you purchase it through his API), he is calling you a serf.

articles.title: npm’s Defaults Are Bad
articles.content_snippet:
Yesterday the axios package was compromised on npm. An attacker hijacked a maintainer account, published two malicious versions that bundled a remote access trojan through a staged dependency called plain-crypto-js, and the versions were live for two to three hours before npm pulled them. Axios gets 83 million weekly downloads. This keeps happening over and over and over and the post-incident conversation always goes the same way: was the maintainer using MFA, should the registry have caught it faster, should people be running more scanners. None of that gets at why JavaScript keeps having these incidents at a rate no other ecosystem comes close to matching. The npm client’s defaults actively enable the attacks and have done for years.
npm install rewrites your lockfile
npm install will modify your lockfile if it detects drift between package.json and package-lock.json, which means the command developers reach for by default, the one in every tutorial and onboarding doc, can silently change your resolved dependency tree. The behaviour you actually want in almost every case lives in npm ci, which refuses to install if the lockfile doesn’t match and never modifies it. Most developers only discover npm ci after something breaks in CI, and many never discover it at all, because the client steers them toward the less safe option by making it the obvious one.
Lifecycle scripts run by default
When you run npm install, every dependency and transitive dependency gets to execute arbitrary code on your machine through postinstall scripts. A vanishingly small number of packages actually need this, mostly native addons that compile C/C++ bindings, but npm grants the privilege to everything by default.
The axios attacker used exactly this mechanism, staging a clean version of plain-crypto-js eighteen hours before publishing a second version with the payload, then adding it as a dependency to the compromised axios release so the RAT dropped automatically on install.

articles.title: Making human languages irrelevant
articles.content_snippet:
If global large-scale human communication continues to be concentrated within large social media platforms and content providers like YouTube, human languages may become sort of irrelevant in that space.
Sometimes I Google for something and see a Reddit result in Finnish. I live in Finland, so it makes sense when the search engine prioritizes such results, but most of the time the actual Reddit thread is not in Finnish at all.

Reddit can translate any thread with a simple URL param e.g. ?tl=fi for Finnish. These dynamically generated pages are somehow indexed by Google, so a thread like this is shown like this instead for me.
Often, a thread from a primarily English-speaking subreddit would randomly contain comments in different languages.


YouTube sometimes serves videos in a language different from your locale and automatically enables AI-powered auto-dubbing. 

I suspect many people never notice these small labels and hidden explanations.

The mixing of different languages in Reddit threads and YouTube comments is probably the result of these automated translations. It is not that someone decided to reply in Spanish to an English thread; rather, they hadn't seen the English thread at all – it was in Spanish for them.
When I play multiplayer online games with proximity voice chat enabled, I often meet people who would just start talking to me in their native language. Perhaps they just get paired with their local players most of the time, so they got used to it. But perhaps people already start expecting that they can speak any language, and the technology somehow takes care of it all? Probably not yet, but we're close. 
This reminds me of the Babel fish from Douglas Adams' The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.

articles.title: My ramblings are available over gopher
articles.content_snippet:
It has recently come to my attention that people need a thousand lines of C code to read my website.


For simpler clients, my server supports gopher:





/* HTML tags, keywords, commands */
h-n {color: #F27;}
/* Values */
h-v {color: #B8F;}
/* CSS selectors, attribute/varable names, file names */
h-s {color: #AEE;}
/* Comments */
h-c {color: #777;}
h-e {color: #F6F;}


# 
telnet
 maurycyz.com 70
/about.txt
...
telnet
 maurycyz.com 70
/
0READ ME FIRST                     /gopherinfo.txt  maurycyz.com   70
i
1Files..........Programs           /programs.map    maurycyz.com   70
1               Rock photos        /misc/rocks.map  maurycyz.com   70
i
0Cool places....on the web         /real_pages.txt  maurycyz.com   70
1               on gopher          /gopherholes.map maurycyz.com   70
i
1Blog...........Projects           /projects/       maurycyz.com   70
1               Tutorials          /tutorials/      maurycyz.com   70
1               Other              /misc/           maurycyz.com   70
1               Photography        /astro/          maurycyz.com   70
.
0Plain text
1Another directory

...

(stuff I don't use)

9Binary data
IImage

Storing metadata in links is weird to modern sensibilities, but it keeps the protocol simple.
Menus are the only thing that the client has to understand:
there's no URLs, no headers, no mime types —
the only thing sent to the server is the selector (file path), and the only thing received is the file. 

# 144 kB if you want to try it.
echo
 /astro/m27/small.jpg
 | 
ncat
 maurycyz.com
 70
 > 
nebula.jpg
That's quite clunky, but there are lots of programs that support it.
If you have Lynx installed, you should be able to just point it at this URL:


gopher://maurycyz.com


... although you will want to put ASSUME_CHARSET:utf-8 in /etc/lynx.cfg because it's not 1991 anymore[Citation Needed]

articles.title: Two Worlds
articles.content_snippet:
In one world, we have Claude Mythos, a model “dramatically” better than Opus 4.6 (surely this is AGI and the endgame, right?). In another world, we have the AI bubble bursting. How can these two things both be true?

If you went back in time to 1850 with a smartphone and a photo printer, you could quickly become a millionaire selling photos. You’d be invited to royal dignitaries palaces to photograph them, taking trains and boats all over the world. Today, you couldn’t make $5 on a street corner with those same tools. There are photographers who become millionaires today, but they do it because they push the craft of photography forward – they do something few others can. They can’t just show up with no special skills and commonplace items.
AI doesn’t replace programmers or artists, it raises the bar for them. With AI: You Can Just Build Things, But So Can Everyone Else 🤍
Anything a person without skill can build with AI is worth very little, because anyone else can build that same thing. However, people with skill can use the same tools and build valuable things, many top photographers in the world today use iPhones.

Capability and value are not the same thing. AI can keep getting better super fast, but the value of anything it produces by itself is low. As the tools improve, the floor rises, but the total size of the market doesn’t.
AI is going to be the major hot button issue of the 2028 US election, and I totally get why people hate it. If the market doesn’t grow but the AI companies do, the only way they did that was by taking value from everyone else. People are very right to ask who we are building this for? Oh, to take value from people like me? I thought we lived in a democracy, can we vote to not build it?
I personally love AI just from a pure desire to meet silicon-based life, and I can’t wait for superhuman models that nobody profits from.

articles.title: Git Diff Drivers
articles.content_snippet:
When I added a diff driver to git-pkgs, most of the work was already done. git-pkgs could parse 29 lockfile formats and extract dependency lists, so wiring that into git’s textconv mechanism was a small addition that turned git diff on a lockfile from 200 lines of resolver noise into a handful of dependency changes. That got me looking at what else people had built on top of git’s diff driver system, and at the 28 built-in drivers that git ships, none of which has made it into any forge or GUI client.
Built-in drivers
The built-in drivers are defined in userdiff.c and activated by setting diff=<name> in .gitattributes. Each one provides two things: a xfuncname regex that git uses to find function or section headers for hunk context, and a wordRegex that controls how --word-diff tokenizes lines.
The full list as of git 2.53: ada, bash, bibtex, cpp (which covers both C and C++), csharp, css, default, dts, elixir, fortran, fountain, golang, html, ini, java, kotlin, markdown, matlab, objc, pascal, perl, php, python, r, ruby, rust, scheme, and tex. The two most recent additions are ini (2.50) and r (2.51). GitHub’s linguist uses these same names for language detection, so if you set *.rs diff=rust in your .gitattributes, both git locally and GitHub’s code view will understand the intent, though GitHub doesn’t actually use the driver for its web diffs.

*.rs diff=rust
*.go diff=golang
*.kt diff=kotlin


Kotlin was proposed as a patch in 2022 and merged. A TypeScript driver PR was submitted and then retracted, though the cpp driver covers enough of TypeScript’s syntax that most people don’t notice. Languages without a built-in driver still get the default driver, which tries a few generic heuristics for function headers but often latches onto something unhelpful. The difference shows up in hunk headers. Without a driver, a change inside a Ruby method might show @@ -10,3 +10,4 @@ end or latch onto a blank line. With diff=ruby, the same hunk header becomes @@ -10,3 +10,4 @@

articles.title: How Do We Get Developers to Read the Docs
articles.content_snippet:
When I reviewed this PR, I had tears in my eyes. We had done it. We had finally created the perfect API. To top it off, the senior developer who worked on it had written documentation to match. No stones were left unturned. I had the code open on one window and the doc on the other. The moment I felt hesitation in the code, the documentation reassured me.
Why do we make two calls to get the... "We are fetching two types of orders to support legacy subscribers..." the documentation answered before I completed my question. This was standard number 15. The one to rule them all. But I still had one question. As the owner of the API, I read the documentation. Will other developers ever think to read it?
How do I get people to want to read the documentation before they use this API? Because in my experience, nobody reads the documentation.
Not to say that documentation is useless, but my mistake was thinking that the people who want to implement the API are interested in documentation at all. For every API ever built, there are two audiences to cater to, and confusing them is where most documentation goes wrong.
The first group is the consumers of the API. The only thing they want to know is: do the endpoints do what I need, and what parameters do they take? They are not reading your documentation like a book. They are scanning it like a menu. They want to find the thing they need, copy the example, and move on.
The second group is the maintainers of the API. The people who need to understand the why behind every decision. Why are there two calls? Why does this endpoint behave differently for legacy users? Why is this field nullable? These are the people who will be debugging at 2am, and they need the full picture.
The worst thing you can do is write one document that tries to serve both audiences equally. You end up with something that's too deep for the first group to skim, and not structured enough for the second group to find it useful.

articles.title: Mr. Chatterbox is a (weak) Victorian-era ethically trained model you can run on your own computer
articles.content_snippet:
Trip Venturella released Mr. Chatterbox, a language model trained entirely on out-of-copyright text from the British Library. Here's how he describes it:

Mr. Chatterbox is a language model trained entirely from scratch on a corpus of over 28,000 Victorian-era British texts published between 1837 and 1899, drawn from a dataset made available by the British Library. The model has absolutely no training inputs from after 1899 — the vocabulary and ideas are formed exclusively from nineteenth-century literature.

Mr. Chatterbox's training corpus was 28,035 books, with an estimated 2.93 billion input tokens after filtering. The model has roughly 340 million paramaters, roughly the same size as GPT-2-Medium. The difference is, of course, that unlike GPT-2, Mr. Chatterbox is trained entirely on historical data.

Given how hard it is to train a useful LLM without using vast amounts of scraped, unlicensed data I've been dreaming of a model like this for a couple of years now. What would a model trained on out-of-copyright text be like to chat with?

Thanks to Trip we can now find out for ourselves!

articles.title: 6o6 v1.1: Faster 6502-on-6502 virtualization for a C64/Apple II Apple-1 emulator
articles.content_snippet:
runs on a 6502 written in 6502 assembly language. 6o6 implements a completely abstracted memory model and a fully controlled execution environment, but by using the host's ALU and providing a primitive means of instruction fusion it can be faster than a naïve interpreter. This library was something I wrote over two decades earlier for my KIM-1 emulator project for the Commodore 64, and relatively recently I open-sourced and discussed it in detail. It runs on just about any 6502-based system with sufficient memory.

For this update I made some efficiency improvements to addressing modes, trimmed an instruction out of the hot path, provided an option for even more control of the 6502 interrupt flag and implemented a faster lane for direct stores to 6502 zero page (as well as the usual custodial and documentation updates). And, of course, any complex library needs a suite of examples, and of course, any update to a complex library demands new examples to play with too.
  
So, given that this year is Apple's 50th anniversary (and, as it happens, my own 50th year of existence personally), what better way to show off a 6502-on-6502 virtualization library than with an Apple-1 emulator ... that runs on the Commodore 64 or Apple II? Now yea, verily, this is hardly the first such example and several others have done something of the sort, but I submit that 6o6 makes our take on it here unique, and as a bit of fun we'll discuss the Apple-1's hardware and look at all that prior 8-bit emulator art for comparison (for the C64 and Apple II and even more exotic systems like the SAM Coupé).



Let's get the technical notes out of the way first and then we'll get to the rogues' gallery. In broad strokes, 6o6 provides a virtual machine on your 6502 computer that itself implements a full NMOS 6502 software core (documented instructions only), written in 6502 assembly language. You provide a harness, which is the VM's sole access to guest memory, and a kernel, which acts as a hypervisor

articles.title: The Roles of Packages
articles.content_snippet:
Greg Wilson’s recent post An E-Bike for the Mind reminded me of Jorma Sajaniemi’s work on the roles of variables. Sajaniemi found that just eleven roles cover nearly all variables in novice programs: stepper, most-wanted holder, gatherer, one-way flag, and so on. As Wilson puts it, types tell you about a variable’s state at rest while roles tell you about its state in motion. Once you learn the roles, you can look at unfamiliar code and immediately recognize the shape of the algorithm from how data flows through it.
Every package in a registry plays a particular role, whether it’s a library your application calls, a tool your build pipeline runs, a daemon your infrastructure depends on, or a firmware blob that makes your hardware work. This holds across all kinds of package managers, from npm and RubyGems to Homebrew, apt, Helm, Terraform Registry, and OpenVSX, and the role tells you more about how a package fits into a system than the name or the README. Two packages in completely different domains, managed by completely different tools, can behave identically because they play the same role.
Code execution
Application. neovim and ffmpeg via Homebrew, httpie via pip, VS Code extensions via OpenVSX, desktop apps via Flatpak or Snap. Standalone programs distributed through a package manager, meant to be run directly rather than imported into other code. The package manager is acting as a software distribution channel rather than a dependency manager. System package managers like apt and Homebrew have always handled this role naturally, while language package managers treat it as an afterthought. Dev tooling like eslint, prettier, rubocop, and cargo-edit are applications too, but they live in a project’s manifest as dev dependencies rather than being installed globally, and no line of application code ever imports them. Some registries distinguish between library and binary packages, though most treat them identically.

articles.title: The rise and fall of IBM's 4 Pi aerospace computers: an illustrated history
articles.content_snippet:
The morning of April 12, 1981, 20 years to the day after Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space, the
Space Shuttle thundered into the Florida sky.
Commander Young and Pilot Crippen were at the controls as the Shuttle ascended on its first flight.
But the launch, like much of the flight, was really under the control of four computers in the avionics bays
one deck below the crew. A fifth computer stood ready to take over in case of a catastrophic computer malfunction.
These computers, Model AP-101B, were part of IBM's System/4 Pi family.

The Space Shuttle AP-101B computer. This unit flew on multiple flights, including STS-38 (1990) and STS-40 (1991). Photo courtesy of RR Auction.

Introduced around 1967, the System/4 Pi family was a line of compact, powerful computers designed for avionics
roles.
The military used these computers in everything from the F-4 fighter and B-52 bomber to
submarine sonar systems and
the Harpoon anti-ship missile.
Other computers in the System/4 Pi family played more peaceful roles in the development of GPS and fly-by-wire flight
controls. In space, System/4 Pi computers controlled Skylab, the first American space station, as well as Spacelab, the reusable
laboratory flown by the Space Shuttle.
Despite the important roles of System/4 Pi computers, information on them is hard to obtain—Wikipedia entirely omits the CC, SP, and ML models.1
However, I received a stack of 4 Pi marketing brochures and articles, so
I can now fill in many gaps in the history of System/4 Pi.
The first generation
The IBM System/360 line of mainframes was introduced in
1964.
System/360 revolutionized the computer industry with the concept of one family of computers
for all applications: business and scientific. The name symbolized that System/360 covered
the full 360º of applications.
The 4 Pi name extended this idea to applications in the 3-dimensional world: 4π is the number of steradians making up a full sphere.

articles.title: Pretext
articles.content_snippet:
Pretext

Exciting new browser library from Cheng Lou, previously a React core developer and the original creator of the react-motion animation library.

Pretext solves the problem of calculating the height of a paragraph of line-wrapped text without touching the DOM. The usual way of doing this is to render the text and measure its dimensions, but this is extremely expensive. Pretext uses an array of clever tricks to make this much, much faster, which enables all sorts of new text rendering effects in browser applications.

Here's one demo that shows the kind of things this makes possible:

The key to how this works is the way it separates calculations into a call to a prepare() function followed by multiple calls to layout().

The prepare() function splits the input text into segments (effectively words, but it can take things like soft hyphens and non-latin character sequences and emoji into account as well) and measures those using an off-screen canvas, then caches the results. This is comparatively expensive but only runs once.

The layout() function can then emulate the word-wrapping logic in browsers to figure out how many wrapped lines the text will occupy at a specified width and measure the overall height.

Once upon a time, self-hosting used to be a cost-effective thing. Is it still a good option for fending off SaaS as the prices keep creeping up?

Today in Tedium: It’s a tough time to be a financially-conscious computer user. We’re living deep in a RAM crisis, and you’ve probably heard the stories about well-spec’ed computers slowly suffering from a nagging case of Unobtainium. Meanwhile, SaaS just keeps SaaSing, with costs adding up (and tech companies getting bigger) every month. In the past, my recommendation for working around SaaS involved buying a mini PC, loading it up with containers, and using those to get work done. But at a time when a 2-terabyte SSD costs 2.5 to 3 times what it did a year or two ago, does that advice still hold? And I’m a nerd—could it be a decent option for a regular user? With that in mind, I decided to dig in. Does turning a mini PC into a little home server make sense in 2026? Let’s find out, together. — Ernie @ Tedium

articles.title: Endgame for the Open Web
articles.content_snippet:
You must imagine Sam Altman holding a knife to Tim Berners-Lee's throat.
It's not a pleasant image. Sir Tim is, rightly, revered as the genial father of the World Wide Web. But, all the signs are pointing to the fact that we might be in endgame for "open" as we've known it on the Internet over the last few decades.
The open web is something extraordinary: anybody can use whatever tools they have, to create content following publicly documented specifications, published using completely free and open platforms, and then share that work with anyone, anywhere in the world, without asking for permission from anyone. Think about how radical that is.
Now, from content to code, communities to culture, we can see example after example of that open web under attack. Every single aspect of the radical architecture I just described is threatened, by those who have profited most from that exact system.
Today, the good people who act as thoughtful stewards of the web infrastructure are still showing the same generosity of spirit that has created opportunity for billions of people and connected society in ways too vast to count while —not incidentally— also creating trillions of dollars of value and countless jobs around the world. But the increasingly-extremist tycoons of Big Tech have decided that that's not good enough.
Now, the centibillionaires have begun their final assault on the last, best parts of what's still open, and likely won't rest until they've either brought all of the independent and noncommercial parts of the Internet under their control, or destroyed them. Whether or not they succeed is going to be decided by decisions that we all make as a community in the coming months. Even though there have always been threats to openness on the web, the stakes have never been higher than they are this time.

articles.title: Using Perfetto in ZJIT
articles.content_snippet:
Originally published on Rails At Scale.
Look! A trace of slow events in a benchmark! Hover over the image to see it get bigger.

Now read on to see what the slow events are and how we got this pretty picture.
The rules
The first rule of just-in-time compilers is: you stay in JIT code. The second
rule of JIT is: you STAY in JIT code!
When control leaves the compiled code to run in the interpreter—what the ZJIT
team calls either a “side-exit” or a “deopt”, depending on who you talk
to—things slow down. In a well-tuned system, this should happen pretty
rarely. Right now, because we’re still bringing up the compiler and runtime
system, it happens more than we would like.
We’re reducing the number of exits over time.
Lies, damned lies, and statistics
We can track our side-exit reduction progress with --zjit-stats, which,
on process exit, prints out a tidy summary of the counters for all of the bad
stuff we track. It’s got side-exits. It’s got calls to C code. It’s got calls
to slow-path runtime helpers. It’s got everything.
Here is a chopped-up sample of stats output for the Lobsters benchmark,
which is a large Rails app:

articles.title: An Intention Upgrade
articles.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
articles.content_snippet:
By ditching the Mac Pro so close to its 50th anniversary, Apple is making a statement of intent for its next 50 years.

A mere six days before the 50th anniversary of Apple, the company quietly did something it has clearly wanted to do for a long time.
It killed the Mac Pro, a device with a lineage that dates back decades. While it has only been a Mac Pro since 2006, its real roots probably lie in the PowerMac G3 Blue & White, the first new tower produced since Steve Jobs’ return to Apple.
That device combined upgradeability with design chops, using a provocative metal-plus-plastic design to create a visual language that was all Apple’s. The most recent Mac Pro, and pretty much every Mac Pro since 2006, has been surrounded in metal. But that was the machine that set the stage for what this top-level Mac was supposed to be: A highly upgradeable screamer.
Again, there is no reason Apple needed to make this decision now. It could have just kept selling the M2 Ultra Mac Pro for a few more years. (Hey, it did it with the trash can.) But the decision to do so just before an important anniversary in its history? That’s sending a message.
The message is simple: We’re not about PCIe ports, we’re about buy-once, upgrade-never devices. Every other device in Apple’s lineup, barring a storage upgrade forced out of the Mac Mini and Mac Studio by clever hardware hackers, has avoided upgrades. And it’s done so for a long time.
The last laptop to offer upgradeable RAM was the 2012 MacBook Pro. It’s been about five years since Apple has offered an iMac or Mac Mini capable of aftermarket RAM upgrades. It’s not like the company was hiding it from us. This is what Apple is: A company that asks you to buy the most powerful machine you can afford up front, and then do it again in five to seven years.

articles.title: Sharing a Name
articles.content_snippet:
My bank card never arrived. I called the bank and, after being redirected through several departments, was assured that it had been mailed. Then we argued a bit about what "7 to 10 business days" meant, we were already on day 14. We ended the call by agreeing to disagree.
Eventually, I did get my card. But it wasn't the mailman who delivered it. Instead, it was my neighbor from two streets down. On the envelope, my address had been crossed out, and the word "incorrect" was handwritten beside it. Why? Because the mailman had done it. You see, I had just moved into the apartment complex, and my name looked familiar to him. Of course he knew who Ibrahima Diallo was, he had been delivering his mail for years. So he corrected it.
In the US, both my first and last name are uncommon (or so I thought). They're often a source of confusion when my Starbucks order gets called out. As it turns out, one of my neighbors shares the exact same name. And on top of that, he uses the same West African spelling: Ibrahima. The mailman, trying to be helpful, had redirected my mail to what he thought was the right address.
My neighbor and I laughed about it. Then I immediately cancelled the card and requested a new one...
Some years ago, I dated a woman from Bulgaria. She grew up in a small city where everyone knew each other. In their town, there was a single Black family. You probably know where this is going, but pretend you don't and follow along.
It was so unusual to have an outsider in this town that the man and his family became local fixtures. Wherever they went, people stopped to take pictures with them. They were like minor celebrities. So naturally, when she pulled out a photo from her childhood, there he was, posing cheerfully with the neighbors.
She turned the photo over to read the names written on the back. She stopped. She burst out laughing. I looked at the name. I can't read Cyrillic, but I know exactly how to spell my name in Bulgarian. His name read: Ibrahima Diallo.

articles.title: How we get radicalized in America
articles.content_snippet:
Be healthy, be young, fall ill. You have a great job of course, you have insurance. It would be ok if the worst thing about health insurance in America was it is hard to navigate. No! The actual problem is that your insurance is incentivized not to cover you at your most vulnerable moment.
You pay them every month. That's money that goes from your paycheck, into their pockets. Now if they cover you, that's money that leaves their pocket, and go into your treatment. There are two ways they can make money. 1. You continue paying every month, and never fall ill. 2. You fall ill, and they deny you care. 
Only the second option is an active option. Health Insurance is a scam that we have normalized in the United States. It helps no one, it makes healthcare unaffordable, and you have to fight tooth and nail to get any sort of care. When Luigi was in the headlines, and news anchors were asking how such a young man can get radicalized, I shook my head. 
In America, it is our tradition to get 2 jobs. It is our tradition to live paycheck to paycheck. And it is our tradition to get radicalized the moment we get sick. When you get sick, the healthcare industry tries to charge much as they can get away with and the insurance industry tries to deny as much as it can.

articles.title: The Top 10 Biggest Conspiracies in Open Source
articles.content_snippet:
10. Dependabot is a surveillance program
GitHub’s Dependabot builds a real-time map of which companies use which software, how quickly they respond to security advisories, and how their internal code review processes work. The pull requests are a side effect of the data collection, and the actual product is the response-time dataset, which correlates strongly with engineering team health and is quietly sold to recruiters through a subsidiary that nobody has been able to identify by name.
The noise volume is calibrated to a specific threshold: just enough PRs to desensitize reviewers to automated contributions, but not so many that they disable it entirely, which is why the PR descriptions are always slightly too long and the changelogs are always included in full even though nobody has ever read one. A former GitHub employee who asked not to be named described the calibration process as “A/B testing, but the B stands for burnout.”
9. The Dockerfile syntax is deliberately broken
The Dockerfile syntax is almost-but-not-quite bash, and the usual explanation is that it was a pragmatic early design decision that became too entrenched to fix. But fixing it would have been a single breaking change in a tool that was already shipping breaking changes every few months in 2013 and 2014, and nobody proposed it, not once, across thousands of GitHub issues, which is unusual for a developer community that will file an issue about a misaligned help flag.
The syntax stayed broken because the broken syntax is what generates the consulting revenue. Every Dockerfile that fails because a developer wrote it like a shell script is a billable hour for someone, and the companies that built their businesses on Docker training and migration services were, by 2015, among Docker Inc’s largest enterprise customers and most vocal community advocates. articles.title: Thoughts on slowing the fuck down
articles.content_snippet:
Thoughts on slowing the fuck down

Mario Zechner created the Pi agent framework used by OpenClaw, giving considerable credibility to his opinions on current trends in agentic engineering. He's not impressed:

We have basically given up all discipline and agency for a sort of addiction, where your highest goal is to produce the largest amount of code in the shortest amount of time. Consequences be damned.

Agents and humans both make mistakes, but agent mistakes accumulate much faster:

A human is a bottleneck. A human cannot shit out 20,000 lines of code in a few hours. Even if the human creates such booboos at high frequency, there's only so many booboos the human can introduce in a codebase per day. [...]

With an orchestrated army of agents, there is no bottleneck, no human pain. These tiny little harmless booboos suddenly compound at a rate that's unsustainable. You have removed yourself from the loop, so you don't even know that all the innocent booboos have formed a monster of a codebase. You only feel the pain when it's too late. [...]

You have zero fucking idea what's going on because you delegated all your agency to your agents. You let them run free, and they are merchants of complexity.

I think Mario is exactly right about this. Agents let us move so much faster, but this speed also means that changes which we would normally have considered over the course of weeks are landing in a matter of hours.

articles.title: Code as a Tool of Process
articles.content_snippet:
Steve Krouse wrote a piece that has me nodding along:
Programming, like writing, is an activity, where one iteratively sharpens what they're doing as they do it. (You wouldn't believe how many drafts I've written of this essay.)
There’s an incredible amount of learning and improvement, i.e. sharpening, to be had through the process of iteratively building something.
As you bring each aspect of a feature into reality, it consistently confronts you with questions like, “But how will this here work?” And “Did you think of that there?”
If you jump over the process of iteratively building each part and just ask AI to generate a solution, you miss the opportunity of understanding the intricacies of each part which amounts to the summation of the whole.
I think there are a lot of details that never bubble to the surface when you generate code from English as it’s simply not precise enough for computers.
Writing code is a process that confronts you with questions about the details.
If you gloss over the details, things are going to work unexpectedly and users will discover the ambiguity in your thinking rather than you (see also: “bugs”).
Writing code is a tool of process. As you go, it sharpens your thinking and helps you discover and then formulate the correctness of your program.
If you stop writing code and start generating it, you lose a process which helped sharpen and refine your thinking.
That’s why code generation can seem so fast: it allows you to skip over the slow, painful process of sharpening without making it obvious what you’re losing along the way.
You can’t understand the trade-offs you’re making, if you’re not explicitly confronted with making them.
A Metaphor
To help me try to explain my thinking (and understand it myself), allow me a metaphor.
Imagine mining for gold.
There are gold nuggets in the hills.
And we used to discover them by using pick axes and shovels.
Then dynamite came along. Now we just blow the hillside away. Nuggets are fragmented into
